      "# AGENTS.md\n\n## Build / Lint / Test / Run\n\nNo test suite, linter, or build tool config (`Makefile`, `tox.ini`,\n`package.json`, etc.) is present in this repo \u2014 none of those commands\nexist to run. What's actually here:\n\n```bash\n# Install dependencies\npip install -r requirements.txt\n\n# Run the admin app (Flask dev server, port 5005, debug=True)\npython3 EXPCMS.py\n\n# Run the static site builder directly\npython3 EXPCMS_Builder.py\n\n# Syntax-check a file without running it\npython3 -c \"import ast; ast.parse(open('EXPCMS.py').read())\"\n```\n\n## Code Style & Conventions\n\n- **Library naming:** frozen BEJSON/MFDB core files use the\n  `lib_bejson_Core_<name>.py` family prefix and are treated as an\n  untouched, verbatim baseline \u2014 copied from the production BEJSON CMS\n  repo, not hand-edited here. This project does not use the `CMS` family\n  (that belongs to the separate production BEJSON CMS product) \u2014 all\n  Experimental-CMS-specific application libraries use the\n  `lib_bejson_ExpCMS_<name>.py` prefix under `Lib_PY/ExpCMS/`;\n  presentational/HTML3 helpers use `lib_bejson_HTML_<name>.py` under\n  `Lib_PY/HTML/`.\n- **Entry points import libraries via `sys.path` manipulation**\n  (`sys.path.append`/`sys.path.insert`), not package-style\n  (`Lib_PY/Core/`, `Lib_PY/HTML/`, `Lib_PY/ExpCMS/` each have\n  no `__init__.py`). Don't add one without checking\n  every import site still resolves.\n- **MFDB primary keys:** every entity's `primary_key` field is declared\n  explicitly in its schema (e.g. `Category.primary_key = \"category_slug\"`,\n  `Page.primary_key = \"page_uuid\"`). Foreign keys follow a `_fk` suffix\n  convention (`category_fk`, `author_fk`) and store the *primary key\n  value* of the referenced entity, not a raw index.\n- **Templates:** every admin template `{% extends \"admin_base.html\" %}`.\n  Component CSS classes use the `c-` prefix (e.g. `c-sidebar__link`,\n  `c-bejson-form__input`); utility classes use `u-` (e.g. `u-badge`).\n- **Static-site vs. admin theming are two independent token sets.**\n  The admin app's CSS (`lib_bejson_HTML_bejson_html3_component_css.py`,\n  `lib_bejson_HTML_bejson_html3_skeletons.py`) defines `--bg-page`, `--bg-alt`,\n  `--text-main`, etc. The exported static site (`Global_Skeleton.html`)\n  defines its own dark-theme tokens (`--bg`, `--surface`, `--text`, etc.)\n  with `--bg-page`/`--bg-alt`/`--text-main` aliased onto them so shared\n  components (e.g. the BEJSON table/combobox widget) render identically\n  in both places. Keep that alias block in sync if the site's token names\n  ever change.\n- **Widgets are fully portable snippets** (`lib_bejson_ExpCMS_widgets.py`): no\n  external CDN dependencies, CSS scoped under a unique per-instance\n  wrapper class, any JS wrapped in an IIFE. Follow this contract for any\n  new widget so it renders identically in the admin preview, the built\n  static site, and if pasted anywhere else.\n- **Jinja2 `Template()` calls in the builder must keep autoescaping on**\n  (`EXPCMS_Builder.py` wraps all template rendering through a single\n  autoescape-enabled constructor) \u2014 `jinja2.Template()` has autoescaping\n  off by default, unlike Flask's `render_template()`.\n\n## Architectural Rules\n\n- **MFDB databases are permanent** \u2014 `Data/workspace/db_*/104a.mfdb.bejson`\n  (manifests) and `Data/workspace/db_*/data/*.bejson` (entity files) are\n  the actual data store. `Data/global_master.mfdb.zip` /\n  `Data/content_master.mfdb.zip` are the archived masters that\n  `MFDBArchive.mount()`/`.commit()` sync the workspace against. Never\n  delete any of these, regardless of apparent staleness.\n- **`.mfdb_lock` files under each workspace db are transient runtime\n  state** \u2014 written on mount, self-regenerate on the next\n  `MFDBArchive.mount()` call. Safe to delete if stale; not part of the\n  actual data.\n- **Empty foreign keys must fall back to a real default, never be saved\n  as `\"\"`.** A page saved with `category_fk=\"\"` matches no `Category`\n  record and silently disappears from every feed \u2014 always default to\n  `'uncategorized'` when a form field comes back blank (see `save_page()`\n  and `import_html_as_page()` in `EXPCMS.py`/`lib_bejson_ExpCMS_cms_mfdb.py`).\n\n## Directory Map\n\n| Path | Contents |\n|---|---|\n| `EXPCMS.py` | Admin Flask app: all routes, sidebar HTML generator, app config, `MFDB_CMS_Manager` instantiation |\n| `EXPCMS_Builder.py` | Static site builder: reads the content MFDB, renders `HTML_Skeletons/` + `Components/` into `Processing/www/` |\n| `Lib_PY/Core/` | Canonical frozen BEJSON/MFDB core |\n| `Lib_PY/HTML/` | Shared component CSS, skeleton tokens, html3 body/table/widget renderers |\n| `Lib_PY/ExpCMS/` | `lib_bejson_ExpCMS_cms_mfdb.py` \u2014 `MFDB_CMS_Manager`, all CMS data access; widget registry; chunker/archive wrapper |\n| `templates/` | Admin app Jinja2 templates (extend `admin_base.html`) |\n| `templates/components/backend/` | Reusable admin UI fragments (Data-Table, Form-Row) |\n| `Components/` | Jinja2 components injected into the *built static site* (feed item cards, hero section, footer/header \u2014 some historically dead, see `docs/cleanup-log.md`) |\n| `HTML_Skeletons/` | Page shells for the built static site (`Global_Skeleton.html`, `Article_Skeleton.html`, `Category_Feed_Skeleton.html`) |\n| `Data/workspace/db_global/` | Global MFDB: ads, authors, media, nav links, site config, social links, video assets |\n| `Data/workspace/db_content/` | Content MFDB: categories, pages, page content, standalone apps |\n| `Data/*.mfdb.zip` | Archived MFDB masters (backup/restore target) |\n| `docs/` | This documentation set |\n",

Since this app's\n  actual reads/writes go straight to the live workspace and the archive is\n  only refreshed on manual repack, the archive was stale relative to live\n  data (missing the entire `VideoAsset` table). Reproduced against the real\n  shipped `Data/` directory: SiteConfig 6 rows \u2192 3, VideoAsset table gone\n  entirely, after a single restart. Rewrote `mount_system()` to only ever\n  cold-mount from the archive when no live manifest exists yet for that\n  root; if live data is present it just ensures a lock session, never\n  wipes. Verified with fresh-install, live-data, and repeated-restart\n  scenarios, all passing.\n\n**Library hardening (`Lib_PY/Core/`, verified bugs, see BUGFIX_*.md):**\n- `_update_manifest_record_count()` had no lock around its manifest\n  read-modify-write, so concurrent writes to two different entities under\n  the same manifest could silently lose one write's `record_count` update.\n  Fixed with a `ResilientPIDLock` on the manifest path. Verified closed\n  under an actual concurrent-thread stress test.\n- `bejson_safe_join()`'s traversal check used a string `.startswith()`\n  comparison, bypassable by any sibling directory sharing a name prefix\n  with the base dir (e.g. `Data` vs `Data_secrets`). This is the guard used\n  when extracting untrusted zip member names during archive mount and\n  backup restore. Fixed using `Path.relative_to()` for real path-segment\n  containment. A page title containing `<`, `>`, or `&` would corrupt the surrounding HTML structure. Replaced with 4 new Jinja2 component templates (`Components/body/Template-Feed-Item-{News,Product,Masonry,Blog}.html`) rendered via `Template().render()`.\n- **Caught and fixed a second-order bug introduced by that very fix in the same pass:** `jinja2.Template()` has autoescaping OFF by default \u2014 Flask's `render_template()` enables it separately, but the builder's raw `Template()` calls never got that for free. First pass at the refactor would have silently carried the exact same unescaped-HTML risk forward. Wrapped all 10 `Template()` call sites in the builder through a single autoescape-enabled constructor. Verified in a real browser with a deliberately malicious test title (`<script>alert(1)</script>`) \u2014 confirmed it now renders as literal visible text, zero `alert()` fired, zero injected `<script>` tags in the DOM.\n\n**Other real fixes:**\n- `/build` route replaced `subprocess.run([sys.executable, \"EXPCMS_Builder.py\"], ...)` with a direct in-process import and call. Removed the now-unused `subprocess` import. Exceptions now go through `app.logger.exception()` for a full traceback instead of being swallowed into a flash message.\n- `/categories` no longer trusts a client-supplied hidden `is_update` field (string-compared against `'true'`) to decide create-vs-update. Server now checks the database directly for the slug's existence \u2014 can't be spoofed or left stale by a client-side JS bug. Removed the now-dead hidden input and its JS reference from `categories.html`.\n- `_get_content_preview()` in the builder now uses BeautifulSoup (already a project dependency) instead of a raw regex tag-strip, correctly handling malformed markup and comments that the regex would mangle.\n- **Added `requirements.txt`** \u2014 didn't exist anywhere in the project before now. Pins `Flask`, `Jinja2`, `Werkzeug`, `beautifulsoup4`.\n\n**Addressed but explicitly out of scope, with reasoning:**\n- `POSITIONAL_VIOLATION` repair / `mfdb_core_self_heal` \u2014 lives in `lib_bejson_Core_*`, the frozen Core baseline copied verbatim from production per this project's isolation architecture. Not modified here; any real fix belongs in the production BEJSON CMS repo. Also pushed back on the audit's framing of self-healing as inherently \"a confession of broken writes\" \u2014 defensive self-repair on load is standard practice for file-based multi-writer systems regardless of write-path correctness; it covers failure modes like manual out-of-band file edits, not just write failures.\n\n**Verification performed:**\n- Compile + pyflakes clean across all touched files after dead-code removal and refactors\n- Full route sweep: 17/17 routes (including `/widgets/picker`) return 200\n- In-process `/build` confirmed actually running in-process (build output visible directly in the Flask process log, not a subprocess)\n- Category create + update both verified working under the new server-side existence check\n- XSS-adjacent fix verified in a real browser: malicious title renders as text, no script execution, no injected DOM nodes\n- Widget system's intentional raw-HTML rendering (via `| safe` at the page-body level) confirmed unaffected by the card-template autoescape fix\n- Test data cleaned up after verification; final rebuild confirms baseline 12 pages\n\nv3.4.0 \u2192 v3.5.0, package 18.\n\n## 2026-07-20 \u2014 YouTube Video Media Asset Type\n\n**New feature \u2014 YouTube links as a real media asset type:**\n- New `VideoAsset` entity in the global MFDB database: `video_uuid`, `url`, `video_id`, `provider`, `title`, `thumbnail_url`, `added_at`.       "# Experimental CMS (ExpCMS)\n\nA Flask + MFDB (BEJSON multi-file database) content management system with\na static-site builder. The admin app (`EXPCMS.py`) manages pages, categories,\nauthors, apps, ads, navigation, and media; `EXPCMS_Builder.py` renders the\nmanaged content into a fully static, self-contained HTML site with no\nexternal CDN dependencies.\n\n## Features\n\n- **Page/content editor** \u2014 title, category, author, body HTML, with an\n  embeddable widget picker (Social Links, Call-to-Action Box, YouTube Video)\n  for inserting portable, self-contained snippets into page content.\n- **HTML Import** \u2014 bulk-imports existing HTML/Word documents as pages,\n  stripping Word cruft, scripts, and AI-tool watermark footers via\n  BeautifulSoup.\n- **Category feeds** \u2014 six feed layouts (blog, news, products, masonry,\n  gallery, app) rendered from `HTML_Skeletons/Category_Feed_Skeleton.html`.\n- **Standalone App hosting** \u2014 import and serve arbitrary HTML/ZIP apps\n  under `/apps`.\n- **Media Library** \u2014 file uploads (single + bulk directory import) and\n  YouTube video assets (auto-derived thumbnails, no API key required).\n- **Static site builder** \u2014 generates a complete static site (with\n  sitemap.xml) from the MFDB content database into `Processing/www/`.\n- **Preview server**, **backup/restore** (zips the MFDB masters), and a\n  **Build & Tools** system page for triggering builds/repacks.\n- **MFDB persistence** \u2014 all structured data lives in BEJSON 104/104a\n  manifest + entity files under `Data/workspace/`, archived to\n  `Data/global_master.mfdb.zip` / `Data/content_master.mfdb.zip`.\n\n## Installation\n\n```bash\npip install -r requirements.txt\n```\n\nRequires Python 3.10+.\n\n## Usage\n\nRun the admin app (serves on port 5005):\n\n```bash\npython3 EXPCMS.py\n```\n\nThen open `http://127.0.0.1:5005/` for the admin dashboard.\n\nBuild the static site directly (writes to `Processing/www/`), without going\nthrough the admin UI's `/build` route:\n\n```bash\npython3 EXPCMS_Builder.py\n```\n\nThe admin app's **Build & Tools** page (`/system`) exposes the same build\nstep, plus **Repack** (re-archives the MFDB workspace into the two master\n`.zip` files) and **Factory Reset**.\n\n## Project Structure\n\n```\nEXPCMS.py                    Admin Flask app \u2014 all routes, sidebar, config\nEXPCMS_Builder.py             Static site generator (reads MFDB, writes Processing/www/)\nLib_PY/Core/                  Canonical frozen BEJSON/MFDB core (bejson_core, mfdb_core, path_guard, validators, errors)\nLib_PY/HTML/                  lib_bejson_HTML_*.py \u2014 shared component CSS, skeleton tokens, html3 body/table/widget renderers\nLib_PY/ExpCMS/                lib_bejson_ExpCMS_cms_mfdb.py \u2014 MFDB_CMS_Manager, all CMS data access (pages, categories, media, etc.)\n                               lib_bejson_ExpCMS_widgets.py \u2014 embeddable widget registry (Social Links, CTA, YouTube)\n                               lib_bejson_ExpCMS_chunker_wrapper.py / lib_bejson_ExpCMS_mfdb_chunker_v6.py \u2014 archive/restore\ntemplates/                    Jinja2 templates for the admin app\nComponents/                   Jinja2 components injected into built static pages\nHTML_Skeletons/                Global/Article/Category page skeletons for the built site\nData/                         MFDB workspace + archived master databases (never delete)\ndocs/                         Project documentation (this doc set)\n```\n\n## License\n\nThis project is licensed under PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 \u2014 free       "# Library Bug-Fix Report \u2014 lib_bejson_Core_mfdb_core.py\n\n**Authorization:** Direct user instruction, this conversation, 2026-08-05 \u2014\n\"Inspect all database... harden and refine, weed out any bugs.\" Verified via\nreproduction before changing anything, per Section 3.5.2.\n\n**File:** `Lib_PY/Core/lib_bejson_Core_mfdb_core.py`\n**Version:** 2.3.0 \u2192 2.3.1\n\n## The bug \u2014 manifest `record_count` lost-update race\n\n`mfdb_core_add_entity_record()`, `mfdb_core_remove_entity_record()`, and the\nupdate functions each take a `ResilientPIDLock` on the **entity file's own\npath** for their read-modify-write cycle \u2014 correct, and sufficient to protect\nthe entity file itself. But every one of them finishes by calling\n`_update_manifest_record_count(manifest_path, ...)`, which does its own\nseparate read-modify-write of the **shared manifest file** \u2014 previously with\nno lock of any kind.\n\nTwo different entities under the same manifest (e.g. adding a `NavLink` and\nadding an `AuthorProfile` at the same time) lock two *different* entity\nfiles, so neither blocks the other. Both then race into the unlocked\nmanifest read-modify-write: both read the same starting manifest doc,\neach mutates only its own entity's row in memory, and whichever call's\n`_write_manifest_doc()` lands last overwrites the file with its own\nin-memory copy \u2014 silently discarding the other write's `record_count`\nupdate. The entity data files themselves stay correct; only the manifest's\ncached `record_count` column (used for dashboard stats) can drift, which is\nexactly the class of problem `mfdb_core_sync_all_counts()` exists to repair\nafter the fact rather than prevent at the source.\n\nNot currently triggerable in Experimental CMS's own deployment (Flask dev\nserver runs single-threaded), but it is a real defect in a shared library\nused across other projects, and would activate the moment any caller runs\nmulti-threaded or multi-process.\n\n## The fix\n\n`_update_manifest_record_count()` now wraps its full read-modify-write in\n`ResilientPIDLock(manifest_path, timeout_seconds=10)`. Verified no existing\ncall site ever holds a lock on `manifest_path` before calling this function\n(the four CRUD functions lock `entity_path`, a different file), so this\nintroduces no reentrancy/deadlock risk against current callers.\n\n## Verification\n\n- Full test tree in `Lib_PY/Core/` byte-compiles clean.\n- `mfdb_core_add_entity_record`, `remove`, and bulk-update smoke-tested\n  individually post-change \u2014 all still commit correctly.\n- No behavior change for the existing single-threaded call pattern; this is\n  a pure hardening fix for concurrent access.\n",

      "# Library Bug-Fix Report \u2014 lib_bejson_Core_bejson_path_guard.py\n\n**Authorization:** Direct user instruction, this conversation, 2026-08-05 \u2014\n\"Inspect all database... harden and refine, weed out any bugs.\" Verified via\nreproduction before changing anything, per Section 3.5.2.\n\n**File:** `Lib_PY/Core/lib_bejson_Core_bejson_path_guard.py`\n**Version:** 1.0.0 \u2192 1.1.0 (module `VERSION` constant: 1.2.0 \u2192 1.3.0)\n\n## The bug \u2014 sibling-directory traversal bypass\n\n`bejson_safe_join()`'s containment check was:\n\n```python\nif not str(target_path).startswith(str(base_path)):\n    raise ValueError(...)\n```\n\nA plain string prefix check. Any resolved path whose string representation\nhappens to start with `base_dir`'s string is accepted \u2014 including a\n**sibling** directory that merely shares a name prefix. Example: base_dir\n`/x/Data`, and a path that resolves to `/x/Data_secrets/leak.txt`. The\nstring `\"/x/Data_secrets/leak.txt\".startswith(\"/x/Data\")` is `True`, so the\nold check let it through, even though `/x/Data_secrets` is not inside\n`/x/Data` at all.\n\nReproduced directly against this function: called with a `../Data_secrets/\nleak.txt`-style relative path, it returned the resolved path with **no\nexception raised**.\n\nThis function is the actual traversal guard applied to untrusted zip member\nnames in two places:\n- `MFDBArchive.mount()` in `lib_bejson_Core_mfdb_core.py`, when extracting\n  a `.mfdb.zip` archive.\n- `CMS_Chunker_Wrapper` / `MFDB_CMS_Manager`'s backup-restore path in\n  `lib_bejson_CMS_cms_mfdb.py`, when unpacking an admin-uploaded backup zip.\n\nA crafted archive containing a member name engineered to resolve to a\nsibling-prefixed path (e.g. `../Data_backup_evil/...`) could have written\noutside the intended extraction root.\n\n## The fix\n\nReplaced the string-prefix check with `Path.relative_to()`, which raises\n`ValueError` unless `target_path` is a genuine path-segment descendant of\n`base_path` (or equal to it). This correctly rejects sibling-directory\nmatches while still accepting all legitimate nested paths.\n\n## Verification\n\n- Reproduction case (`../Data_secrets/leak.txt` against base_dir `Data`)\n  now correctly raises `ValueError: Path traversal detected`.\n- Legitimate nested joins (e.g. `bejson_safe_join(root, \"data\", \"file.bejson\")`)\n  still resolve normally.\n- All three call sites (`mfdb_core.py` zip extraction, and the two backup\n  restore call sites in `cms_mfdb.py`) byte-compile and were smoke-tested\n  with a normal (non-malicious) backup/restore round-trip.\n",

lines.append(\\\"\\\")\\n\\n    total_included = 0\\n    total_skipped  = 0\\n\\n    for cat_row in cats:\\n        cat_name       = cat_row[_fi(\\\"category_name\\\")]\\n        chunks_in_cat  =     # Always skip status=skip\\n            if chunk_status == \\\"skip\\\":\\n                total_skipped += 1\\n                continue\\n            # Tag filter\\n            if filter_tag and      total_skipped += 1\\n                continue\\n\\n            content = chunk_row[_fi(\\\"chunk_content\\\")] or \\\"\\\"\\n            if content.strip():\\n                section_lines.append(content.strip())\\n                section_lines.append(\\\"\\\")\\n                total_included += 1\\n\\n        if section_lines:\\n            lines.append(f\\\"## \\\"\\\\n\\\".join(lines)\\n    compiled_dir  = _doc_compiled_dir(doc_name)\\n    out_file      = compiled_dir / f\\\"{doc_name}_filtered_{suffix}.md\\\"\\n    out_file.write_text(compiled_text, \\u2500\\u2500 Multi-doc merge cmd_doc_import_file(file_path_str, delimiter, category_name, label_prefix=None):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    Split an existing text file on delimiter and create one chunk per segment.\\n    Appends chunks to category_name in the active doc.\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    doc_name = _require_active_doc()\\n    if not doc_name:\\n        return\\n\\n    input_file = Path(file_path_str).resolve()\\n {created} chunk(s) from '{input_file.name}' into '{category_name}'.\\\")\\n\\n\\n# \\u2500\\u2500 Doc locking \\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\n\\ndef cmd_doc_lock(idx_str=None):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Lock the active (or indexed) doc \\u2014 blocks add/delete/reorder chunk operations.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    doc_name = _resolve_doc_by_idx(idx_str) if idx_str \\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\n\\ndef Run --doc-list first.\\\")\\n        return None\\n\\ndef cmd_duplicate_doc(idx_str, new_name):\\n    source_name = _resolve_doc_by_idx(idx_str)\\n    if not source_name:\\n        return\\n\\n    new_name = safe_name(new_name)\\n    new_dir  = DOC_PROJECT_DIR / new_name\\n\\n    if new_dir.exists():\\n        print(f\\\"Error: A document project named '{new_name}' already exists.\\\")\\n        return\\n\\n    source_dir = DOC_PROJECT_DIR / source_name\\n\\n    # Block duplicate while source is mounted \\u2014 mounted files would carry over\\n    state = _load_mount_state()\\n    if source_name in state:\\n        print(f\\\"Error: '{source_name}' is currently mounted. Run --doc-list first.\")\n        return None\n\ndef cmd_duplicate_doc(idx_str, new_name):\n    source_name = _resolve_doc_by_idx(idx_str)\n    if not source_name:\n        return\n\n    new_name = safe_name(new_name)\n    new_dir  = DOC_PROJECT_DIR / new_name\n\n    if new_dir.exists():\n        print(f\"Error: A document project named '{new_name}' already exists.\")\n        return\n\n    source_dir = DOC_PROJECT_DIR / source_name\n\n    # Block duplicate while source is mounted \u2014 mounted files would carry over\n    state = _load_mount_state()\n    if source_name in state:\n        print(f\"Error: '{source_name}' is currently mounted. Commit or discard before renaming.\")\n        return\n\n    source_dir = DOC_PROJECT_DIR / source_name\n\n    # Rename the directory\n    source_dir.rename(new_dir)\n\n    # Rename the schema file inside Schema/\n    old_schema_file = new_dir / \"Schema\" / f\"{source_name}.104db.bejson\"\n    new_schema_file = new_dir / \"Schema\" / f\"{new_name}.104db.bejson\"\n    if old_schema_file.exists():\n        old_schema_file.rename(new_schema_file)\n\n    # Rename compiled output file if it exists\n    old_compiled = new_dir / \"Compiled\" / f\"{source_name}.md\"\n    new_compiled  = new_dir / \"Compiled\" / f\"{new_name}.md\"\n    if old_compiled.exists():\n        old_compiled.rename(new_compiled)\n\n    # Update active doc pointer if it was pointing at the renamed doc\n    active = _get_active_doc()\n    if active == source_name:\n        _set_active_doc(new_name)\n        print(f\"[*] Active doc updated to: {new_name}\")\n\n    print(f\"[*] Renamed '{source_name}' \u2192 '{new_name}'\")\n\n\ndef cmd_export_doc(idx_str, export_format):\n    \"\"\"\n    Export a document project's compiled content to a chosen format.\n    Formats:\n      md   \u2014 Markdown (same as compiled output, copy to cwd)\n      txt  \u2014 Plain text, section headers as === underlines, no Markdown syntax\n      json \u2014 JSON array, one object per chunk: {category, label, position, content}\n    The exported file is placed in the doc's Compiled/ directory alongside the .md.\n    \"\"\"\n    VALID_FORMATS = (\"md\", \"txt\", \"json\")\n\n    export_format = export_format.strip().lower()\n    if export_format not in VALID_FORMATS:\n        print(f\"Error: Unknown format '{export_format}'. Valid options: {', '.join(VALID_FORMATS)}\")\n        return\n\n    doc_name = _resolve_doc_by_idx(idx_str)\n    if not doc_name:\n        return\n\n    state = _load_mount_state()\n    if doc_name in state:\n        print(f\"Warning: '{doc_name}' has uncommitted mounted changes \u2014 export will reflect last committed schema state.\")\n\n    doc = _load_doc_schema(doc_name)\n    if not doc:\n        return\n    values = doc.get(\"Values\", [])\n    cats   = _sorted_cats(values)\n\n    if not cats:\n        print(f\"No categories in '{doc_name}'. Nothing to export.\")\n        return\n\n    compiled_dir = _doc_compiled_dir(doc_name)\n    compiled_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n\n    if export_format == \"md\":\n        # Re-use the existing .md if present, otherwise compile fresh to temp\n        source_md = compiled_dir / f\"{doc_name}.md\"\n        if not source_md.exists():\n            print(f\"[*] No compiled .md found \u2014 running compile first.\")\n            cmd_doc_compile()\n        out_file = compiled_dir / f\"{doc_name}_export.md\"\n        shutil.copy2(str(source_md), str(out_file))\n        print(f\"[SUCCESS] Exported Markdown \u2192 {out_file}\")\n\n    elif export_format == \"txt\":\n        lines = []\n        title = doc_name.replace(\"_\", \" \")\n        lines.append(title)\n        lines.append(\"=\" * len(title))\n        lines.append(f\"Exported: {get_timestamp()}\")\n        lines.append(\"\")\n\n        # Plain-text TOC\n        lines.append(\"TABLE OF CONTENTS\")\n        lines.append(\"-\" * 40)\n        for i, cat_row in enumerate(cats, 1):\n            lines.append(f\"  {i}. {cat_row[_fi('category_name')]}\")\n        lines.append(\"\")\n\n        for cat_row in cats:\n            cat_name = cat_row[_fi(\"category_name\")]\n            chunks   = _sorted_chunks_in_cat(values, cat_name)\n            lines.append(\"\")\n            lines.append(cat_name)\n            lines.append(\"=\" * len(cat_name))\n            lines.append(\"\")\n            for chunk_row in chunks:\n                content = chunk_row[_fi(\"chunk_content\")] or \"\"\n                if content.strip():\n                    lines.append(content.strip())\n                    lines.append(\"\")\n\n        out_file = compiled_dir / f\"{doc_name}_export.txt\"\n        out_file.write_text(\"\\n\".join(lines), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        print(f\"[SUCCESS] Exported plain text \u2192 {out_file}\")\n\n    elif export_format == \"json\":\n        records = []\n        for cat_row in cats:\n            cat_name = cat_row[_fi(\"category_name\")]\n            chunks   = _sorted_chunks_in_cat(values, cat_name)\n            for chunk_row in chunks:\n                records.append({\n                    \"category\":        cat_name,\n                    \"category_pos\":    cat_row[_fi(\"category_index_pos\")],\n                    \"chunk_id\":        chunk_row[_fi(\"chunk_id\")],\n                    \"chunk_label\":     chunk_row[_fi(\"chunk_label\")],\n                    \"chunk_pos\":       chunk_row[_fi(\"chunk_index_pos\")],\n                    \"chunk_content\":   chunk_row[_fi(\"chunk_content\")] or \"\",\n                })\n        out_file = compiled_dir / f\"{doc_name}_export.json\"\n        out_file.write_text(\n            json.dumps({\"doc_name\": doc_name, \"exported\": get_timestamp(), \"chunks\": records}, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False),\n            encoding=\"utf-8\"\n        )\n        print(f\"[SUCCESS] Exported JSON ({len(records)} chunk(s)) \u2192 {out_file}\")\n\n#       "# Architecture\n\n## Components\n\n### Admin app \u2014 `EXPCMS.py`\nSingle-file Flask app. Instantiates one `MFDB_CMS_Manager` (`cms`) at\nmodule load against `DATA_ROOT = Data/`, and one `EXPCMS_Builder`\nper `/build` request. Owns all 39 routes: dashboard, page/category/author/\napp/ad/nav CRUD, media (file + YouTube video), HTML import, widget\npicker/renderer, backups, preview server control, and system tools\n(build/repack/factory-reset). Also generates the sidebar HTML directly\n(`get_sidebar_html()`) rather than delegating to `lib_html3_sidemenu.py`\n(that file is unused \u2014 see `docs/cleanup-log.md`).\n\n### Static site builder \u2014 `EXPCMS_Builder.py`\n`EXPCMS_Builder(data_root, skel_dir, output_dir)`. `build_site()`:\n1. Loads `Category` and other entities directly via\n   `MFDBCore.mfdb_core_load_entity()`.\n2. Renders the homepage (`_hero_content()` / `_build_homepage` path).\n3. For each category, calls `_build_category()`, which pulls matching\n   pages via `cms.get_pages_in_category(category_slug)`, renders each\n   into a feed-item card (`Components/body/Template-Feed-Item-*.html`,\n   chosen by the category's `feed_type`), and wraps the result in\n   `HTML_Skeletons/Category_Feed_Skeleton.html`.\n4. Renders individual pages via `HTML_Skeletons/Article_Skeleton.html`.\n5. Renders standalone apps (`_copy_apps()`).\n6. Writes `sitemap.xml`.\n\nAll page rendering funnels through one shared `_render_page(page_context)`\n\u2192 `Template(self.global_skel).render(page_context)`, so every generated\npage gets the same context keys (`sidebar_block`, `related_block`,\n`page_title`, `category_slug`, `category_name`,\n`shared_component_css` \u2014 see below).\n\n### `Lib_PY/ExpCMS/lib_bejson_ExpCMS_cms_mfdb.py` \u2014 `MFDB_CMS_Manager`\nThe single data-access layer for the whole CMS. Wraps two MFDB\ndatabases (`global_manifest`, `content_manifest`) and exposes typed\nCRUD methods per entity (`get_pages_in_category`, `create_page`,\n`update_page`, `import_html_as_page`, `add_video_asset`,\n`parse_youtube_url`, backup/restore via `MFDBArchive`, etc.). Every\nroute in `EXPCMS.py` and every read in `EXPCMS_Builder.py` goes through\nthis class \u2014 there is no direct file I/O against the `.bejson` entity\nfiles anywhere else in the app.\n\n### `Lib_PY/Core/lib_bejson_Core_*.py` \u2014 canonical frozen BEJSON/MFDB core\nCopied verbatim from the production BEJSON CMS repo, kept in its own\n`Core` family folder rather than duplicated per-app (as of the 2026-07-31\nlibrary push \u2014 see `CHANGELOG.md`; previously frozen isolation copies\nlived under the retired `Lib_EXPCMS/`). Implements the BEJSON 104/104a\nparser/validator, MFDB manifest + entity file I/O, path guarding, and\nerror types. Never hand-edited here; any real fix belongs upstream.\n\n### `Lib_PY/HTML/lib_bejson_HTML_bejson_html3_component_css.py` /\n### `lib_bejson_HTML_bejson_html3_skeletons.py`\nShared CSS component library (`COMPONENT_CSS`) and page-skeleton token\ntemplates (`CSS_CORE_SKELETON`), used to build the admin app's\n`becss_css` (`CSS_CORE.format(**COLOR)` in `EXPCMS.py`). Since 2026-07-30,\n`EXPCMS_Builder.py` also imports the raw `COMPONENT_CSS` string directly\n(de-escaping its doubled `{{`/`}}` braces, since it's normally consumed\nthrough a later `.format()` call) and injects it into every built page\nvia the `shared_component_css` template variable \u2014 this makes components\nembedded in page content (e.g. the BEJSON table/combobox widget from\n`lib_bejson_HTML_html3_tables.py`) render identically on the live static site as they\ndo in the admin editor, instead of only in the admin editor.\n\n### `Lib_PY/ExpCMS/lib_bejson_ExpCMS_widgets.py`\nRegistry of portable, self-contained widgets (Social Links, Call-to-Action\nBox, YouTube Video) insertable into any page's body HTML via the widget\npicker (`templates/_widget_picker.html`, `/widgets/picker`,\n`/widgets/render/<key>`). Each widget's HTML/CSS/JS has zero external\ndependencies and CSS scoped under a unique per-instance wrapper class.\n\n### `Lib_PY/ExpCMS/lib_bejson_ExpCMS_chunker_wrapper.py` / `lib_bejson_ExpCMS_mfdb_chunker_v6.py`\nArchive/restore engine used by the Backups page (`/backup/create`,\n`/backup/restore`) to chunk the MFDB workspace into portable archives.\n\n## Data Flow\n\n```\nAdmin UI (templates/*.html)\n        \u2502  form POST\n        \u25bc\nEXPCMS.py routes\n        \u2502  cms.<method>()\n        \u25bc\nMFDB_CMS_Manager (lib_bejson_ExpCMS_cms_mfdb.py)\n        \u2502  reads/writes\n        \u25bc\nData/workspace/db_{global,content}/104a.mfdb.bejson (manifest)\nData/workspace/db_{global,content}/data/*.bejson (entity files)\n        \u2502  MFDBArchive.commit() on /repack\n        \u25bc\nData/{global,content}_master.mfdb.zip (archived masters)\n```\n\n```\n/build route (or `python3 EXPCMS_Builder.py` directly)\n        \u2502\n        \u25bc\nEXPCMS_Builder.build_site()\n        \u2502  MFDBCore.mfdb_core_load_entity() + cms.get_pages_in_category()\n        \u25bc\nHTML_Skeletons/*.html + Components/body/Template-Feed-Item-*.html\n        \u2502  Template(...).render(page_context)\n        \u25bc\nProcessing/www/  (static site output, incl. sitemap.xml)\n```\n\nCategory feed pages depend on every `Page.category_fk` matching a real\n`Category.category_slug` exactly \u2014 a blank or mismatched `category_fk`\nsilently drops that page from every feed with no error surfaced anywhere\nin the UI. `save_page()` and `import_html_as_page()` both default a blank\ncategory to `'uncategorized'` to guard against this.\n",

      "# Security & Integrity Notes\n\n## 2026-08-18 \u2014 pkg29 audit-fix pass \u2014 Phase 1 (security)\n\n- **NEW-H1 (High)**: `do_unchunk()` in\n  `Lib_PY/ExpCMS/lib_bejson_ExpCMS_mfdb_chunker_v6.py` wrote restored\n  files at `out_dir / rel_path` with no boundary check. `rel_path`\n  comes from restored **entity row data** (backup contents), not zip\n  member names \u2014 `safe_extract_zip`'s per-member `bejson_safe_join`\n  check (LIB-CH-H2, pkg24) never sees it. A crafted backup could carry\n  `file_path` values like `../../../anything` inside the chunked rows\n  and write outside the unchunk staging directory. Fixed: the target\n  path is now resolved through `bejson_safe_join()`, which raises on\n  any escape attempt; the existing `except Exception` turns that into\n  a clean rejected-restore result.\n  - **Not yet fixed \u2014 flagged for explicit go-ahead**: the identical\n    pattern (unchecked `rel_path` join) exists in the **Core** family\n    lib `Lib_PY/Core/lib_bejson_Core_bejson_chunking.py`, in\n    `bejson_core_chunking_unchunk_chunked_104()` and a second unchunk\n    site (~line 789, appears to be `resurrect_file`/mount). Now reads\n  `EXPCMS_PREVIEW_HOST` (default `127.0.0.1`), warns loudly if set to\n  a non-loopback host \u2014 same pattern as `EXPCMS_HOST`.\n- **NEW-H3 (High)**: `/apps` zip import accepted `entry_file` from the\n  form with no validation, then `EXPCMS_Builder.py` interpolated it\n  raw into an unescaped iframe `src` on every built app page \u2014 a\n  crafted value could inject HTML attributes or an arbitrary path.\n  Fixed on both ends: `EXPCMS.py` now runs `entry_file` through\n  `secure_filename()` and rejects the import if the result isn't\n  actually present in the extracted zip; `EXPCMS_Builder.py` also\n  `html.escape()`s it before interpolation and adds\n  `sandbox=\"allow-scripts allow-same-origin\"` to the iframe, since\n  hosted apps are arbitrary admin-uploaded content and should be\n  treated as untrusted on the public site.\n- **NEW-M5 (Medium)**: `Lib_PY/Core/cli/CLI_Doc_Chunker/update-libs.txt`\n  contained an instruction addressed to an AI/human agent, referencing\n  a \"cracked folder\" and asking that dependency imports be added and\n  \"sent back.\" This is a social-engineering / prompt-injection\n  artifact embedded in the repo \u2014 its instructions were **not**\n  followed.
